focus: Flaky vs real classification of the four failing workflows, timeout-minutes inventory and sizing, and the carried-forward vitest fileParallelism question
answeredQuestions: Which tests or jobs are flaky or slow, and are job timeouts set and sized right?

graphEvents.label: Which tests or jobs are flaky or slow, and are job timeouts set and sized right?
Deep-loop failures are real STALE_SOURCE_DIGEST after ~12 min of job time
No fail-then-pass flake signature anywhere in the dataset
Failures are correlated across independent workflows on the same commits
27 of 33 workflows set no timeout-minutes, inheriting the 360-minute default
Set timeouts are 4-12x oversized and never approached

label: The 13/40 deep-loop-runtime failures are real, not flaky: sampled logs (runs 39843480132, 39025144155) both end in 'Refusing stale compiled contract for deep/ai-council: STALE_SOURCE_DIGEST', i.e. a committed source change without a regenerated contract; the job spends ~11.7 of its ~11.7 minutes before reporting, while compile-command-contracts.cjs already supports a verify-only invocation (--write is opt-in), so the same fact is obtainable in seconds as a first step.

No flake signature exists in the measured data: the 1000-run window holds 947 success / 35 skipped / 17 failure with zero timed_out and zero cancelled runs, only 2 same-commit groups were ever rerun (both after a failure), and every same-commit repeat in the 40-run samples of the seven failing workflows is success/success - the fail-then-pass-on-one-commit transition occurs zero times. Retry-to-green is not in use and would have nothing to fix.

Failures are correlated across independent workflows on the same commits (356f614, aa152a4, 13209a6, 7584ad7 fail diagram-corpus and skill-advisor-stress together; b4d4e90, 66e432f, 0efd5a1, 3c66787, 91c7486 fail deep-loop-runtime and diagram-corpus together), and the sampled causes are content assertions ('version 1.0.1.0 is outside the anchor's 1.2 era' in run 39406017176; 'TypeError: default is not a function' in 4 of 64 tests of run 39524217211) - repo-state defects that a retry would mask rather than fix.

27 of 33 workflows declare no timeout-minutes at all, so any hang inherits GitHub's 360-minute per-job default; the missing set includes spec-kit-check's 20-minute check job and the nightly strict-pass-freshness job whose slowest observed execution is 4262 s (71 min) with four more placements at 2863/2568/2038/1660 s. Timeout coverage, not tuning, is the gap.

The six workflows that do set timeout-minutes size them 3.9x to 11.5x above their own median job time (deep-loop-runtime 2700 s vs 690 s, hooks-node-tests 1200 vs 194, opencode-plugin-tests 1200 vs 138, opencode-dual-version 1800 vs 156, skill-advisor-stress 1200 vs 115, sk-doc-rename-harness 1800 vs 172), no job has come within 3x of its ceiling and zero runs timed out - the generous-but-bounded shape is correct and should be copied onto the other 27 rather than tightened.

The carried-forward question is answered in the negative: no vitest config sets fileParallelism true - system-spec-kit runtime, its two projects, system-skill-advisor runtime and system-deep-loop runtime all set false to serialize shared-state fixtures (graph writer lock, temp project roots), with testTimeout a uniform 30 s and teardownTimeout 1 s. So the fixture-collision risk is already handled, and the serialization is exactly the wall clock seen in the 688-698 s deep-loop job and the 167-file spec-kit-check lane.

Failure cost in runner minutes is negligible - roughly 10 billed min/day for deep-loop-runtime (13/40 failures x ~11.5 min over 15 days) and 1-2 min/day for the other three flagged workflows against a ~3812 billed min/day total - so a 32.5% failure rate on a 12-minute job hurts through reviewer trust and signal latency, not spend. Ranked consequence: add a cheap freshness gate first, do not build retry automation.
A red workflow is only evidence of a flake when the same commit fails and then passes; without that transition, retries hide a real defect.
Every job needs a bounded ceiling no more than ~12x its median, because an unset ceiling is a 6-hour runner hold on a hang.

direction: Add workflow-level retry/rerun automation for the four failing workflows
reason: zero fail-then-pass transitions in 1000 runs and in all 40-run samples; failures are commit-correlated across independent workflows, so a retry reproduces the same content defect and delays the fix

direction: Set fileParallelism true to recover wall clock in the deep-loop and spec-kit suites
reason: all five configs disable it deliberately for shared-state fixtures (graph writer lock, temp project roots); enabling it trades a known determinism guarantee for parallel-wall-clock without evidence the suites are isolated
